strengths: Principled taxonomy-driven dataset curation addressing previously overlooked perspective-taking capabilities; SenseNova-SI-8M (8.5M QA pairs) systematically combines existing data with 4.5M strategically generated samples

Comprehensive empirical validation across five spatial benchmarks (VSI, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, SITE), multiple model families (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel), and model sizes demonstrating consistent improvements

Rigorous robustness analysis including circular tests (10-point drop vs. 30+ for baselines), VSI-Debiased evaluation, no-vision ablations (85.6%→52.5% drop), and frame extrapolation (trained on 16 frames, generalizes to 32+) providing strong evidence of genuine spatial reasoning
Broad model scope showing generalization across diverse architectures and pretraining paradigms; downstream validation on embodied AI tasks (EmbodiedBench) demonstrates practical applicability
Clear presentation with effective visualizations; commitment to open-source release of models and code benefits community reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: work is primarily data-centric scaling without introducing new architectures, training techniques, or reasoning mechanisms; core approach is straightforward dataset curation + training existing models

Performance saturation without forward direction: Figure 1 shows clear diminishing returns; authors acknowledge 'data scaling alone is unlikely to achieve human-level' performance and that paradigm shifts are needed, but provide no concrete proposals

Chain-of-Thought analysis disappointing (Section 5.6): all three CoT variants yield only ~2% typical gains, with best variant improving only 8.6% on specific subset; acknowledged as insufficient to justify computational overhead, suggesting text-based reasoning fundamentally limited for spatial understanding

Critical ablation studies missing: no analysis of data balance between dominant capabilities (MM/SR) vs. underrepresented (PT/MR); no component-wise evaluation showing which capabilities drive improvements; no source-level contribution analysis

Perspective-taking (PT) improvements unconvincing: despite positioning PT as critical, ViewSpatial benchmark (PT-focused) achieves only 54.6% vs. 68.7% on broader VSI-Bench; 13.1% gap suggests PT remains significantly harder, contradicting claims of targeted improvement

Data generation quality inadequately documented: 4.5M synthetic samples lack quality metrics, inter-annotator agreement scores, or detailed generation procedures; potential biases in 3D source datasets (ScanNet, Matterport3D) not discussed

Emergent capabilities claims under-supported: 'spill-over' (Fig. 3) based on two anecdotal examples without systematic ablation; 'extrapolation' interesting but not unprecedented and may reflect encoder properties rather than true emergent reasoning

Incomplete baseline comparisons: concurrent works (VST, Cambrian-S) marked with † use cited results rather than reproductions; comparison with proprietary models not under authors' control makes attribution difficult
Statistical rigor lacking: formal significance tests absent despite varied improvement magnitudes (0.72% to 154.4%); confidence bands shown but p-values not provided for critical claims
Manuscript status unclear: abstract states 'this report will be updated continuously,' suggesting evolving work rather than finished submission inappropriate for formal venue

Limited theoretical insight: lacks analysis of why spatial intelligence benefits from data scaling, relationships between spatial capabilities, or fundamental limits of scaling approaches; no investigation into why CoT approaches fail
Narrow evaluation scope: all evaluation on indoor scenes and object manipulation; generalization to outdoor navigation, large-scale environments, or other spatial domains unexplored
Training details sparse: single epoch mentioned without justification; data sampling strategy (balanced vs. natural) unclear; sensitivity to data composition unexplored

strengths: Systematic and principled data curation addressing key gaps (especially perspective-taking), yielding 8.5M diverse samples organized under a well-motivated cognitive taxonomy
Comprehensive evaluation across five recent spatial benchmarks (VSI, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, SITE) with strong results competitive with proprietary models and clear ablations/breakdowns
Rigorous robustness analysis including circular tests, no-vision tests, and debiased benchmarks that convincingly demonstrate genuine spatial reasoning rather than language shortcuts
Extensive empirical analysis of scaling laws, emergent generalization (spillover, extrapolation), and cross-architecture validation (Qwen3-VL, InternVL3, Bagel)
Thorough retention of general capabilities (MMBench-En, MMStar, AI2D, OCRBench) showing training on spatial data doesn't cause catastrophic forgetting
Strong commitment to reproducibility with detailed training specs, code/model release, and comprehensive appendices enabling community replication
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: contribution is primarily data-centric (scaling existing models on curated data) with no architectural innovations or new training paradigms; curation practices follow established approaches

Saturation observed without solutions: performance plateaus significantly after ~5-6M samples (Fig. 1, Table 7); paper acknowledges data scaling alone insufficient but offers no path forward; vague claims about 'paradigm shifts' lack substance

Chain-of-Thought results underwhelming: all three CoT variants yield only ~2% gains with 1000-2000+ token overhead; analysis is preliminary with tentative hypotheses rather than insights into why text-based reasoning fails for spatial tasks

Dataset contribution lacks transparency: exact breakdown of 8.5M samples across capabilities missing; inter-annotator agreement, quality metrics for auto-generated QA pairs, and validation procedures not reported; unclear how much improvement stems from existing vs. newly curated data

Emergent capability claims overstated: spillover within perspective-taking is expected transfer; extrapolation from 16→32 frames shows modest gains (~4%) with degradation beyond 64 frames; interesting but incremental findings

Inadequate ablation studies: no direct removal of PT data to quantify its specific contribution; fairness of comparisons unclear (VST/Cambrian-S achieve less improvement with comparable data—why?); cross-dataset transfer not analyzed

Downstream evaluation limited to single task (embodied manipulation) without comparison to other spatial approaches; absolute success rates remain modest (16.6%→33.3%); unclear why this task specifically benefits or how findings generalize

Missing systematic failure analysis: while robustness tests validate visual grounding, analysis of which spatial reasoning types remain hard is absent; Figure 6 c,d failures lack categorization and deeper investigation
Statistical rigor concerns: no confidence intervals or significance tests; standard deviations shown only in radar charts; single training runs without reported variance across seeds

Scope and presentation issues: paper reads as technical report rather than research contribution; framing as 'ongoing project' atypical for CVPR; dense 33-page submission; some vague claims about 'unprecedented performance' require qualification

strengths: Systematic, principled approach using EASI taxonomy for decomposing spatial intelligence into core capabilities
Large-scale curated dataset (8M samples) with sophisticated filtering and image selection pipeline
Strong empirical results across 5 diverse benchmarks, surpassing GPT-5 on perspective-taking (80.7% vs lower performance)
Rigorous robustness evaluation including circular tests, VSI-Debiased evaluation, and no-vision controls demonstrating genuine visual grounding
Comprehensive analysis of scaling behaviors, emergent generalization, and single-dataset training necessity
Multi-architecture validation (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel) demonstrating approach generalization
Public commitment to release models, code, and dataset, providing significant community value
Downstream validation on embodied AI without finetuning (+59.6% success rate improvement)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—primarily data-centric scaling without architectural innovation or modifications to base models
Preliminary and inconclusive CoT analysis showing only 2-7% gains; proposed hypotheses are speculative rather than conclusive
Saturation plateau effects (Fig 1) suggest fundamental limitations of scaling-only approaches; paper acknowledges but doesn't address paradigm shift needed
Synthetic data quality control procedures underspecified: validation methodology, error rates, and manual verification extent not reported for 4.5M generated samples
Data contamination prevention not explicitly discussed despite combining diverse multi-source datasets; risk of train-test overlap unclear
Limited failure mode analysis—Section 5.7 shows failures but provides no systematic breakdown or generalizable insights
Generalization concerns: predominantly indoor scene training (ScanNet-based); modest SITE performance (47.7%) suggests distribution specificity
Training setup inadequately justified: single-epoch training rationale unexplained, learning rate arbitrary (5×10⁻⁶), no statistical significance testing or error bars reported
Missing ablations on dataset composition, data mixture sensitivity, and impact of individual spatial capabilities
Dense presentation (33 pages) with normalized radar charts obscuring absolute performance differences; CoT notation inconsistently applied
